assembly.land_count_status: Physical solderable lands, not assembler-approved chargeable joint count. DNP, bare PCB features, copper-only Kelvin taps and paste subdivisions excluded.
assembly.xray_count_status: Hardware audit:20 IC packages with hidden/exposed pads; assembler decides actual sampling, frames and chargeable package count.
assembly.attrition_status: Engineering planning allowance, not supplier acceptance: small passives reserve minimum20 pieces per MPN per order (two side setups at10 pieces), other SMT minimum1 or10%, THT minimum1 or5%. Actual per-side feeder/library MOQ can be larger.
assembly.procurement_route: Public distributor prices plus overseas consignment to assembler. Consignment acceptance, import eligibility and lead times not confirmed. No blanket global-sourcing markup added as well.

allowance_status: Unverified engineering unit budget ranges, NOT manufacturer/distributor prices and NOT evidence of an available substitute. No volume discount invented for unpriced parts. Multiply by planned purchase quantity including spares.

notes: All service ranges above are engineering budget allowances; they are not JLC quotes or published local labor rates.
Programming assumes a released test image and5/10/20USD labor per board; firmware development excluded.

Electrical test assumes30/50/100USD per board for continuity, current-limited power-up, rail checks, communication and representative dummy loads. It does not include engine, environmental, EMC or full-energy qualification.
Fixture NRE is a provisional bench harness and adapters budget, not a complete automotive production test station.
Logistics includes distributor-to-assembler and assembled-board delivery budget; destination quote, taxes, import duties and brokerage are not known.
Contingency applies to manufacturing subtotal excluding logistics and first fixture NRE. It covers price refresh, supplier process and sourcing uncertainty, not taxes.

exclusions: VAT, import duties, brokerage and destination-specific taxes: unknown, not zero-rate assumptions
